name: cacheclosure
description: Detect GitHub Actions cache identities that are mechanically invariant to repository inputs which can change cached state, using file resolution and shell control-flow witnesses.
tagline: Prove when cached state can change without changing its key.

permissions.filesystem: reads GitHub Actions workflow files and repository-local scripts and inputs; writes nothing to the analysed repository
permissions.environment: CACHECLOSURE_PREFIX is read only by install.sh and uninstall.sh

tests.coverage: 95.7% of cacheclosure/core.py executable lines in the frozen suite; 2/3 pinned historical defects recovered and both recovered witnesses cleared by their historical repairs

security.reviewed_by: Frozen CacheClosure v0 protocol; GitHub Actions run 31850105648 passed Ubuntu and macOS on 2026-08-15.

highlights: Proves when a literal hashFiles contribution resolves to zero repository files.
Tracks cached file sentinels into later shell steps and requires a real unkeyed repository input before reporting.
Uses historical human repairs as external oracles; a language model is not part of the decision.
Keeps a known runtime-only defect as a frozen miss instead of broadening the heuristic after seeing the result.

verifications.method: Three preregistered historical repositories, repaired-counterpart controls, 95% coverage gate, asymmetry death threshold at 25%, and a four-job Ubuntu/macOS Python matrix.
verifications.findings: Recovered 2/3 historical defects; the two recovered witnesses disappear on the exact human repair commits; Yapboard remains the preregistered runtime-metadata miss; verify/find median ratio 7.9%.
